messages:

Subject: Pseudonymization approach + SCCs / UK-IDTA alignment

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for the detailed call earlier. As part of our procurement checklist for the EU pilot, Legal has asked for two discrete confirmations before we proceed to procurement sign-off: whether the SCC-based addendum you propose + the pseudonymization controls you described will be adequate for (1) EU -> US processing under the SCCs and (2) a UK-IDTA bridging approach for UK-resident data.

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will perform reversible pseudonymization or tokenization for the requested data elements, and where the key material resides?
- We need an evidence matrix that maps the SCCs clauses and UK-IDTA equivalents to the technical mitigations (e.g., onshore cache fallback, prefix/KV caching behavior, and escrowed logging for audit).
- Any subprocessors that touch plaintext identifiers during training/inference (and their country locations).

I attached the annotated SCCs the legal team prefers and a short list of items we need in a matrix. If you can provide a proposed matrix and a brief note on whether the UK-IDTA addendum is needed for this customer (Medisol prefers single stream documentation if possible), that would be helpful.

We are hoping to close this by end of next week (25 Jan).

Best,
Asha
Data Protection Officer
Medisol Health Systems

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pseudonymization approach + SCCs / UK-IDTA alignment

Hi Asha — thanks for the note and the annotated SCCs, very helpful.

Short answers up front:
- Pseudonymization approach: Redwood can support a deterministic tokenization layer for identifiers (one-way hash with keyed salt managed in customer KMS) or reversible encryption where customers prefer key custody. By default for hosted customers we recommend keyed hashing (non-reversible) for PID elements that do not need reconstitution.
- Key material: if Medisol wants non-reversible tokenization, Redwood holds the salt in a per-customer key store; if reversible encryption is required, we can support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) so keys never leave Medisol control.
- Subprocessors: none of Redwood’s training vendors receive customer plaintext in our hosted inference flow. Our inference subprocessors (monitoring, analytics, CDN) only receive telemetry and token counts — we will include a marked-up subprocessor table in the matrix.

Action plan I propose:
1) We’ll draft the evidence/mapping matrix that ties SCCs articles -> technical mitigations -> audit artifacts (logs, escrows, retention).
2) Kimberly will add the infra-level description (onshore cache fallback and KV cache behavior) and a suggested sampling plan for proof-of-processing.
3) Naomi will scope what additional artifacts we can reasonably provide in a TIA/DTIA (e.g., code-level attestations vs. runtime logs).

I’ve attached a first-pass pseudonymization matrix (pseudonymization-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short spec for the escrowed logging we can provide (onshore-cache-escrow-log-spec.md).

We can do a short review call tomorrow 20 Jan at 9:00 PT if that works for you. If not, we’ll incorporate written comments and aim to send the updated matrix by EOD 22 Jan.

Thanks — Markus
Head of Legal Partnerships (on rotation)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pseudonymization approach + SCCs / UK-IDTA alignment

Asha / team — adding a couple of technical clarifications so the matrix is actionable for your engineering and security teams.

Notes for the matrix:
- Tokenization/encryption: if Medisol selects customer-managed KMS, encrypted identifiers are only reconstitutable within a dedicated on-prem or VPC deployment; we will not rehydrate in hosted shared tenancy.
- Onshore cache fallback: we support a configurable onshore cache (region pinned) for latency-sensitive inference. Cache logs include request id, model id, shard id, timestamp, and anonymized token histogram. Full request payloads are not persisted in the onshore cache logs — they are written to an escrow vault (encrypted at rest) only under audit request.
- Escrowed logs: the escrow spec includes a retention window (default 90 days) and HSM-wrapped export for audited disclosures. Access to escrow exports requires documented DPA/TIA request and a chain-of-access approval.
- Subprocessors sampling plan: we can provide a quarterly attestation plus artifact samples (redacted) that show no plaintext transfer to analytics vendors.

Open question: for UK-IDTA — if you need a separate addendum vs. relying on SCCs + organizational measures, we’ll flag any deviations in the matrix. Our legal team has a short checklist to determine whether the addendum is necessary; in many cases the SCCs + KMS custody + escrow controls are sufficient, but some customers still want the UK addendum paper trail.

I’ll update the XLSX with the infra rows and push a new version by EOD 21 Jan.

—Kimberly
Principal Security PM, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

Markus / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turn. The level of detail in the attachments looks promising. A couple of follow-ups before we route to procurement:

- Please indicate whether the escrow export process requires a binding legal request (signed by Medisol legal) or whether Redwood can initiate an on-demand export under an agreed SLA. Medisol’s security policy requires legal sign-off for any log export containing identifiers.
- For the subprocessor attestation samples: can you provide one redacted sample set (log + attestation) before procurement to satisfy our internal review?
- DocuSign: Legal can accept SCCs with your annotated mapping as long as we have clarity on key custody. If we proceed with customer-managed KMS, can you circulate the DocuSign template for the KMS clause?

If you can confirm the above and send the updated XLSX (with the infra rows and a short note on whether UK-IDTA addendum is required for our configuration) we’ll route for legal procurement review. Our target remains 25 Jan for the procurement packet — a tight timeline but achievable if we get the artifacts today.

Best,
Asha
DPO, Medisol
